title: 5.0 magnitude earthquake strikes Egypt
facts: A magnitude 5.0 earthquake struck off Egypt early on Monday, August 3, 2026.
The United States Geological Survey reported the Egyptian earthquake occurred at 3 a.m. local time (0000 GMT).
The epicenter of the earthquake was located approximately 22 miles (36 kilometers) northeast of the city of Suez.
The German Research Centre for Geosciences (GFZ) measured the earthquake at a magnitude of 5.4.
The German Research Centre for Geosciences recorded the depth of the Egyptian earthquake at 6 miles (10 kilometers).
The Egyptian Red Crescent activated its emergency response plan in the affected governorates.
No casualties were immediately reported following the earthquake in Egypt.
No property damage was immediately reported after the earthquake near Suez.
Humanitarian organizations advised Egyptian residents to avoid buildings showing signs of structural damage.
Damaging earthquakes are uncommon in Egypt.
Egypt's deadliest modern earthquake occurred in October 1992.
The October 1992 earthquake in Cairo measured magnitude 5.8.
The 1992 Cairo earthquake killed more than 500 people.
The 1992 Cairo earthquake displaced thousands of people.
The August 3, 2026 earthquake struck near Egypt's seaport city of Suez.
